text:
jordan: quick follow-up from the CP split spike: we need to pick a long-term approach for regionalizing the control plane for Private customers. tradeoffs: egress cost + latency vs cert propagation, consistency windows, and operator complexity.
lee: tl;dr: regional CP reduces inter-region peering egress and gives lower latency for region-bound tenants, but makes cert + secret sync harder.
carla: agree. another axis: how do we surface a single customer identity if they hit different regional CP nodes? the current model assumes a global subject for audit.
marco: proposal A: 'masterless replicas' 
- each region runs a writable CP instance for tenants pinned to that region
- conflict resolution via per-tenant leader lease and optimistic versioning
sasha: downside: leader lease churn on leader failover, lease traffic across regions to elect leader if tenant moves -> more cross-region traffic.
lee: proposal B: 'regional read replicas + global leader' 
- writes go to global control plane (hosted), reads served locally
- less write-consistency issues but write latency for region-bound writes still hits global.
jordan: both have pros/cons. we considered a hybrid: stick new tenants to a regional leader, but keep global authority for sensitive ops (cert signing, billing).
carla: important: cert signing must be auditable and crash-safe. We cannot leak signing keys to all regions. what about a regional signer that gets short-lived signing tokens from global KMS?
marco: that's what I sketched during spike: global KMS issues scoped token to regional signer with TTL 60s. regional signer can sign ephemeral certs for connections without contacting global for every request.
sasha: sounds reasonable. but what about offline scenarios (customer on-prem Private where control plane region temporarily unreachable)? regional signer needs to be able to sign autonomously for failover window. that implies we must provision a 'resume token' with expiry and limited scope.
lee: security risk: longer-lived resume tokens increase blast radius if compromised. we should limit scope to tenant-id + signing-capabilities and rotate quickly. also logging backchannel needed for replay protection.
jordan: replay protection could be handled by attaching monotonic counters and requiring incremental ack to global control plane when connectivity restored. messy but doable.
carla: operator concerns: on upgrades we must avoid dual-signing windows where the same subject could get conflicting cert serials from two versions of signer. add a migration lock: signer obtains upgrade lease from global before can sign after upgrade.
marco: we also need to think about certificate revocation. CRLs are slow; we should prefer short TTL certs and real-time revocation via control plane push to regional proxies.
sasha: agree. short TTL (30-60s) + push revocation notices. will increase signing rate and load on KMS/token service. plan for autoscaling signer pool.
lee: performance: benchmark shows regional signing with token cache can sign ~1500 certs/s per instance. with 95th percentile latency ~12ms. OK for bursty but we must avoid per-request signing for high-throughput data plane flows. cache ephemeral certs per-session.
jordan: data-plane session affinity: use regional sticky session for tenants by default, fall back to global if affinity broken. that reduces signing churn.
carla: rollout strategy? propose opt-in pilot with 3 customers in eu-west-1 and us-west-2. monitor metrics: cross-region egress, signer QPS, failed leader elections, cert rejection rate.
marco: failure modes to plan:
- signer out of sync -> regional certs rejected -> tenant downtime. mitigation: automatic failback to global CP and alert.
- resume token leak -> revoke via global rotation and short TTLs.
- heavy mount of writes in regional leader -> promote additional replicas (but careful with routing).
sasha: ops asks: need a runbook for emergency global takeover (how to pin tenants to global CP) and a dashboard tile for signer errors + token churn.
infra-bot: created ticket OPS-8124: add regional-signer metrics + emergency failback runbook. ETA 2w.
lee: decision candidate: go hybrid with regional writable leaders for tenant-local ops, global authority for signing + billing. implement regional signer that obtains short TTL tokens from global KMS and supports a limited resume-token for brief offline windows. enforce short cert TTLs and push revocation.
jordan: i like that. two constraints to add: 1) per-tenant opt-in gating (customers must approve regionalized control plane) 2) clear SLA differences documented in onboarding.
carla: approved with caveats. action items:
- marco: prototype regional-signer token exchange and resume-token behaviour (spike 1wk)
- lee: instrument egress + signer QPS dashboards (OPS-8124)
- sasha: draft runbook for emergency failback + cert revocation flow
- jordan: update onboarding copy to include opt-in and SLA deltas
marco: will start spike tomorrow. dropping initial notes into the RFC thread.
carla: thanks all. if anyone has objections to the hybrid path, speak up now or we'll lock this in and start pilot. :white_check_mark:
